A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Neural Interactive Proofs, with readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices. Earlier Appendices A–D correspond to later Appendices B–E; v2 adds a related-work appendix.

before.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D report original graph-isomorphism and APPS-based code-validation experiments, including accuracy, robustness, training analyses and interaction transcripts.

after.justification: Section 6 and Appendix E retain original experiments and supplementary analyses, with several revised plotted results.

M1.justification: The NIP, MNIP and zero-knowledge protocols retain their algorithmic components and objectives. Architectures, PPO training and standard/stabilised expert iteration are unchanged. Revisions to formal assumptions do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic graph-isomorphism pairs and APPS-derived correct/buggy Python solutions, retaining the same graph-size and programming-difficulty coverage. The new regression lemma is theoretical, not an added evaluation task.

E2.justification: Graph comparisons retain ADP, debate, NIP and MNIP with random-prover controls. Code comparisons retain ADP, debate, MAC, NIP and MNIP plus the solo verifier. The updated Waldchen citation refers to the same MAC comparator.

E3.justification: Reported sample sizes, graph generation, 80:20 and 90:10 splits, architectures, metrics, PPO settings, eight expert-iteration rounds and stabilisation schedule are unchanged. Revised plotted values do not establish changes to these protocols.

E4.justification: Existing analyses of verifier capacity and trained-versus-random provers, stabilised training, and per-instance accuracy distributions receive revised evidence in Figures 2b, 4 and 10. Their questions and experimental factors remain unchanged, as do the dataset-size, zero-knowledge coefficient, difficulty and transcript analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions describe error bars as one standard deviation across 10 seeds, retain the graph-training seed count, and use 10 rollouts per code-validation test instance. No uncertainty-reporting practice or statistical test is added or removed.

E6.justification: Figure 2b reverses the displayed trained-versus-random-prover ordering. Figure 4 revises stabilised ADP accuracy from approximately 61% to 80%, acceptance from 20% to 52%, and always-fail percentage from 19% to 3%, making ADP the highest-accuracy interaction protocol in that comparison. Figure 10 substantially changes ADP's post-training histogram and revises several untrained distributions. These are reported-result revisions; the PDFs do not explain whether they reflect corrections or reruns.

T1.justification: Definition 6 revises the capability and objective-misalignment conditions of v1's Definition 5. Proposition 2 becomes Proposition 9 with rho-worst-case robustness and a rho(D) + epsilon bound; its proof replaces the faulty square-root-delta probability accounting with a delta/2 union bound. New Lemma 19 supplies regularity conditions and a proof involving compactness, Lipschitz continuity and distributional support. Table 1 also replaces MAC's unknown complexity classification with MA.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and discussion retain the same central claims: a unifying framework, new interactive-proof protocols including zero knowledge, theoretical and empirical comparisons, and a supporting codebase.

C2.justification: New Appendix A clarifies applicability boundaries by contrasting query-only verification with white-box guarantees and distinguishing the work's data and misalignment assumptions from AI control. Existing experimental explanations and Section 7 limitations remain unchanged, including passages not reconciled with the revised ADP results.

D1.justification: v1 promises a later public code release and refers to supplementary code. v2 supplies an explicit repository address and states that it provides dataset links and generation code, including access to additional prompts. Implementation settings otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A substantially expands positioning through four discussions: scalable oversight, computational asymmetry and complexity theory, formal verification, and learned communication. It adds numerous works and substantive comparisons with AI control, rational proofs and white-box verification. Section 1.3 also revises its description of Kirchner et al.'s training.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. v2 adds a dedicated related-work appendix and acknowledgments, refines explanatory wording, and renumbers formal statements and existing appendices. Retained material is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Most histogram panels in Figures 9–10 gain hatching and more explicit training labels, with adjusted ticks and spacing. Table 1 changes its first-column heading from Model to Protocol, and conference headers and local reflow alter layout. The same 17 figures and two numbered tables are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves theoretical precision, repairs Proposition 9's probability argument, supplies explicit code-access information and substantially clarifies research positioning. Figure 2b now agrees with the accompanying trained-prover claim. These benefits are tempered by unreconciled experimental prose: Section 6.2 still describes stabilisation effects as small despite ADP's revised accuracy, while Appendix E.2.1 overlooks its newly displayed bimodal collapse. The net gain is meaningful but limited.
